styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small wooden chair seen from the front, about 12x20 source px. It has 9 distinct colours and a median of 7 per full tile. That is a little below the hedge (10 per tile, 11 colours) and the bench (14 colours), but a chair this small has fewer pixels to spend. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no dead 5x5 areas. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown, like the wood it borders, and does not read as a black sticker line. The wood has about 4 lightness steps (light seat and slats, mid, dark, and the tinted outline), against about 5 on the bench. The slats and seat carry some grain and edge highlights. It is slightly simpler than the references but not flat or sticker-like, and a careful artist would accept it next to the bench.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small ladder-back chair. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown and follows the wood tone, which matches Beodeul practice. It has no flat 5x5 fills (0% coverage). It is thinner than the references on shading and detail. It has only 9 distinct colours against 14 for the wood bench, and the wood ramp reads as about 4 steps against the bench's 5-6. The back slats and seat are mostly two or three tones with little grain or per-plank highlight. Its per-tile median of 7 is below the hedge (10) and well below the stall (17) and well (20). On a piece this small and simple that gap is modest, but it still looks slightly flatter and more sticker-like beside the bench. When in doubt, fail.
